content.text: Last Lesson: Question Forms and Responses
We reviewed how to form open and closed questions.
You learned to use “wh-” words, auxiliaries, and tag questions.
We practiced giving short, polite, and extended responses.
Turn this sentence into a question: “She visited London last year.”
What’s the difference between “Who did you call?” and “Who called you?”
Respond naturally: “Do you enjoy watching documentaries?”
Numbers are not just for math — they’re essential in daily communication: dates, time, prices, documents, addresses, and more.
To give accurate information, describe sequences, talk about statistics, or share personal/contact info.

What time is it? It’s ______ past seven.
